services.name: api-gateway
services.responsibility: Single entry point for all client traffic. Routes requests, terminates TLS, enforces rate limiting and authentication token validation before forwarding to downstream services.
api_boundaries: ALL /api/v1/** -> routed to appropriate downstream service
risks: Single point of failure if not deployed with redundancy
Becomes a bottleneck if rate limiting / auth checks are not cached

services.name: user-management-service
services.responsibility: Registration, authentication (JWT issuance), profile management, address book, role management.
risks: Password/credential leakage if hashing/storage is misconfigured
PII exposure across service boundaries if not masked in logs

services.name: product-catalog-service
services.responsibility: Manages product listings, categories, pricing, inventory count (read-optimized), and search.
services.database: PostgreSQL (system of record) + Elasticsearch (search index, eventually consistent)
services.tech_notes: Spring Boot, Spring Data JPA; catalog changes published to a 'product-updated' event topic
risks: Search index can drift from source of truth (eventual consistency lag)
High read volume during flash sales requires caching (Redis/CDN) to avoid DB overload

services.name: cart-service
services.responsibility: Manages shopping cart state per user/session: add/remove items, quantity updates, coupon application (validation delegated to Order/Promotion logic).
services.tech_notes: Spring Boot; cart is intentionally not the system of record for price/stock -- always revalidated at checkout
risks: Stale price/stock shown in cart if catalog isn't re-checked at checkout
Concurrent modification of the same cart from multiple tabs/devices

services.name: order-management-service
services.responsibility: Creates orders from validated carts, orchestrates the checkout saga (inventory reservation -> payment -> confirmation), tracks order status and history.
services.tech_notes: Spring Boot; implements the Saga pattern (choreography via events) to coordinate inventory reservation and payment without distributed transactions
risks: Distributed transaction consistency across catalog (stock), payment, and order records
Duplicate order creation on client retries without idempotency keys

services.name: payment-service
services.responsibility: Executes payment authorization/capture via a licensed payment gateway (e.g., Stripe/Razorpay), records transaction state, handles refunds.
services.database: PostgreSQL (transactions, refunds) -- no raw card data stored (PCI-DSS SAQ-A via tokenization)
services.tech_notes: Spring Boot; deterministic, rule-based logic only. See ADR-003 -- AI is explicitly excluded from generating or altering payment decision logic.
risks: Financial loss from incorrect double-charge or failed idempotency handling

cross_cutting_concerns: Centralized auth via JWT validated at API Gateway and re-verified at each service
Distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry) across all services for observability
Idempotency keys required on all state-mutating POST endpoints (Order, Payment)
Structured JSON error model shared across all services
risks_overall: Network latency and partial failure handling between microservices
Operational overhead of running 6 independently deployable services vs a monolith
Need for a saga/compensation strategy since 2-phase-commit is not used across services
